The profile likelihood gives confidence intervals of parameters and predictions of nonlinear models
without a quadratic approximation [@raue2009structural; @kreutz2012likelihood]. Guide:
[Profile likelihood](guide-profiles.html), [Prediction uncertainty](guide-prediction-uncertainty.html).

## Profile and threshold

The [objective]{#def-objective} function $\ell(\theta) = -2 \log L(\theta) - 2 \log \pi(\theta)$ is the
[data term]{#def-data-term} $-2 \log L$ plus the [prior term]{#def-prior-term} $-2 \log \pi$ of the
prior $\pi$ ([Likelihood and prior](methods-objective.html)). `normL2()` returns the data term as
attribute `data`, `constraintL2()` the prior term as `prior`, and `profile()` keeps both as columns.
The [profile]{#def-profile} of $\theta_i$ is $\ell$ minimized over all other parameters as a
function of $\theta_i = c$. The minimizing values of the other parameters form the
[parameter path]{#def-parameter-path} $\hat\theta(c)$,

$$\hat\theta(c) = \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\theta \,:\, \theta_i = c}\, \ell(\theta) , \tag{1}$$

and the [profile likelihood]{#def-profile-likelihood} is the objective along this path,

$$\mathrm{PL}_i(c) = \ell\bigl(\hat\theta(c)\bigr) . \tag{2}$$

A parameter that moves with $\theta_i$ along the path compensates the change of $\theta_i$ in the
predictions (`plotPaths()`).

Without a prior, (2) is the minimum of $-2 \log L$ with $\theta_i = c$. By the likelihood ratio
test, the rise $\mathrm{PL}_i(c) - \mathrm{PL}_i(\hat\theta_i)$ from the optimum $\hat\theta_i$ below
the [threshold]{#def-threshold}, the $1 - \alpha$ quantile of $\chi^2_1$ (3.84 for 95 %), defines an
asymptotic [confidence interval]{#def-confidence-interval}, the set of values $c$ compatible with the data,
invariant under reparameterization of $\theta_i$. The optimum is the minimum of (2).
`profileThreshold()` computes the threshold, `method = "F"` the
[finite-sample threshold]{#def-finite-sample-threshold} $n \log(1 + F_{1,\nu,1-\alpha}/\nu)$ with $n$
data points and $\nu = n - p$ for $p$ estimated mean parameters, exact for Gaussian errors with one
estimated standard deviation. A prior wide against the data curvature keeps (1) finite where the
data do not determine $\theta_i$ and changes (2) little where they do.

`profile()` stops on (2) by default; `stepControl = list(stop = "data")` ends a profile at the
threshold of the data term $-2 \log L\bigl(\hat\theta(c)\bigr)$ along the path, and
`confint(val.column = "data")` reads the interval off that term.

## Shapes

A parameter is [identifiable]{#def-identifiable} when (2) exceeds the threshold on both sides, otherwise
[non-identifiable]{#def-non-identifiable}: [practically non-identifiable]{#def-practical-non-identifiability}
when the profile stays below the threshold on one side or both for the given data,
[structurally non-identifiable]{#def-structural-non-identifiability} when different parameter values give
the same prediction of every observable and the profile is flat
([Structural identifiability](methods-symmetries.html#structural-identifiability)). A
[symmetry]{#def-symmetry} is a transformation of the parameters that leaves every observable unchanged; a
[gauge]{#def-gauge} fixes coordinates so that each orbit of the symmetry meets the fixed values in one
point ([Gauge and reduction](methods-symmetries.html#gauge-and-reduction)).

| shape of (2) | meaning |
|---|---|
| above the threshold on both sides | finite interval |
| below the threshold on one side | practically non-identifiable |
| exactly flat | structurally non-identifiable, a symmetry ([Symmetries](guide-symmetries.html)), removed by a gauge |

On the log scale, a one-sided profile towards $-\infty$ means the reaction can be switched off,
towards $+\infty$ that the process is in equilibrium on the time scale of the data, replaceable by a
large fixed value or the quasi-steady state. Both limits give a
[reduced model]{#def-reduced-model}, the model with the parameter at the limit, with the same fit
[@maiwald2016driving]. Each profile tests one limit with all other parameters free; several limits
together need a likelihood ratio test of the reduced model.

## Computing a profile

A profile is a sequence of constrained fits, each started from the last point.

- `method = "optimize"` steps $\theta_i$ and refits the others with `trust()`, one converged fit
  per point.
- `method = "integrate"`, the [integration-based profile]{#def-integration-based-profile}, follows
  the [constrained optimum]{#def-constrained-optimum} $\hat\theta(c)$ of (1), the stationary point of
  the Lagrangian $\ell(\theta) + \lambda\,(\theta_i - c)$, where $\nabla \ell + \lambda e_i = 0$ and $\theta_i = c$.
  Differentiating in $c$ gives the [path equation]{#def-path-equation}, the linear system for
  $\mathrm{d}\theta/\mathrm{d}c$ that the profile follows in Euler steps,

  $$\begin{pmatrix} H & e_i \\ e_i^\top & 0 \end{pmatrix}
    \begin{pmatrix} \mathrm{d}\theta/\mathrm{d}c \\ \mathrm{d}\lambda/\mathrm{d}c \end{pmatrix}
    = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} \tag{3}$$

  with the Hessian $H$ of $\ell$: one evaluation and one linear solve per step. The step solves (3)
  with $-\gamma \nabla \ell$ in place of the upper zero, which pulls it back to the constrained
  optimum ($\gamma = 1$ by default, adapted to the size of the pull). With a Gauss-Newton $H$ the
  path still drifts, so each step is then corrected by a short fit of the other parameters with
  `trust()`, at most `optControl$iterlim = 10` iterations; `algoControl = list(reoptimize = FALSE)`
  leaves out the fit.

Step control and stops:

| rule | setting |
|---|---|
| step shrinks | mismatch of predicted and actual change above `atol` |
| step doubles | mismatch below `0.3 * atol`, or below `0.3 * rtol` relative |
| side ends | objective (or data term, `stop = "data"`) up by the threshold; `limits` relative to the optimum reached; `limit` steps |

A point of $\ell$ below the start value is a better optimum: fit and profiles are then to be repeated
from it. Where
the curvature jumps, the step shrinks to `min` and stays on the profile.

## Prediction profiles

A prediction $z = g(t, \theta)$ has the [prediction profile likelihood]{#def-prediction-profile-likelihood},
the objective minimized under the constraint $g(t, \theta) = z$,

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{PPL}(z) &= \ell\bigl(\hat\theta(z)\bigr) , \\
\hat\theta(z) &= \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\theta \,:\, g(t, \theta) = z}\, \ell(\theta) ,
\end{aligned} \tag{4}$$

whose threshold gives a confidence interval of the prediction [@kreutz2012likelihood], over several
$t$ a pointwise confidence band. Without a prior the interval is the image of the
[parameter region]{#def-parameter-region} at the $\chi^2_1$ threshold, the set of $\theta$ with
$-2 \log L$ less than 3.84 above the minimum, not of the [joint region]{#def-joint-region}, which uses
the $\chi^2_p$ quantile of all $p$ parameters at once and is larger.

A [validation data point]{#def-validation-data-point}, a hypothetical measurement $v$ of the prediction
with standard deviation $\sigma_v$, makes $z$ a parameter $v$, tied to the prediction by

$$\left( \frac{g(t, \theta) - v}{\sigma_v} \right)^2 . \tag{5}$$

The [validation profile]{#def-validation-profile}, the profile of $v$, is (4) for $\sigma_v \to 0$ and
lies below (4) otherwise. The interval of $v$, the range of a new measurement compatible with model
and data, is therefore wider: for a quadratic (4) of half-width $w$ the half-width becomes $(w^2 + \Delta \sigma_v^2)^{1/2}$,
$\Delta$ the threshold. `datapointL2()` builds (5) as an `objfn` from the evaluation of `normL2()`, which
therefore predicts at $t$ (`times = t`). With `attrName = "data"`, (5) adds to the data term, so
`stop = "data"` and `confint(val.column = "data")` include it. Where the model cannot follow $v$,
(5) grows and ends the profile.
